'''Haim Hanani''' ({{Langx|he|חיים חנני}}; {{Birth date|1912|9|11|df=y}} as '''Chaim Chojnacki'''&ndash; 8 April 1991)<ref>[https://data.bnf.fr/en/17226189/haim_hanani/ BnF: Haim Hanani (1912-1991)]</ref> was a Polish-born Israeli mathematician, known for his contributions to [[Combinatorics#Design theory|combinatorial design theory]], in particular for the theory of [[Combinatorial design#pairwise balanced design|pairwise balanced designs]] and for the proof of an existence theorem for [[Steiner system|Steiner quadruple systems]].<ref name=hanani>{{cite book |title=Combinatorial Designs: A Tribute to Haim Hanani |author=Hartman, A. |isbn=9780444881151 |lccn=lc89023148 |series=Annals of Discrete Mathematics |url=https://archive.org/details/combinatorialdes0000hart |url-access=registration |year=1989 |publisher=Elsevier Science}}</ref><ref name=ams>{{cite journal |journal=Notices of the AMS |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |page=686 |volume=42 |issue=6 |title=Deaths|department=Mathematics People|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199506/people.pdf|date=June 1995 }}</ref> He is also known for the [[Hanani–Tutte theorem]] on [[Crossing number (graph theory)|odd crossings]] in [[planar graph|non-planar graphs]].

==Life==
Hanani (Chojnacki) was born in [[Poland]], studied in Vienna and Warsaw, and graduated with an M.A. from the [[University of Warsaw]] in 1934. He emigrated to the [[Mandatory Palestine|British Mandate of Palestine]], later to become [[Israel]], in 1935 and in 1938 received the first Ph.D. in Mathematics from the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].

In 1955 he was appointed to the faculty at [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology|Technion Institute of Technology]] and from 1969 to 1973 he served as the rector of [[Ben-Gurion University of the Negev|Ben-Gurion University]] in [[Beersheba]]. In 1980 he was awarded the title of Professor Emeritus at that institution.<ref name=hanani/>

His early research led to the proof of the theorem devised by [[R. M. Wilson|Richard M. Wilson]] on pairwise balance designs.<ref name=hanani/>

He wrote scholarly papers with [[Andries Brouwer]], [[Paul Erdős]], [[Alexander Schrijver]], and [[R. M. Wilson|Richard M. Wilson]], among others.<ref>{{cite web |title= Haim Hanani List of Publications |publisher=Leibniz-Zentrum für Informatik |url= http://dblp.dagstuhl.de/db/indices/a-tree/h/Hanani:Haim.html |accessdate=10 November 2012 }}</ref>

His papers were published in journals such as ''[[Discrete Mathematics (journal)|Discrete Mathematics]]'', the ''[[Journal of Combinatorial Theory]]'', the ''[[European Journal of Combinatorics]]'', and the ''[[American Mathematical Monthly]]''.<ref name=hanani/>
